text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
OfficialRussian(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.

Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegister(x) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTaiwan(x)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (OfficialRussian(x) ∧ CitizenshipTaiwan(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(CitizenshipTaiwan(vladimir) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(vladimir)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(ekaterina) ∨ OfficialRussian(ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.

Conclusion:
CanRegister(ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election or is a manager at Gazprom.
